body.statement: For every \((\mathbf X_n,P_{\beta,n})\in\mathfrak M\), every realized bounded potential-outcome table and every pilot-measurable \(\delta_m\), \(E[\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}_{n,m}(\delta_m)\mid\mathbf Y_n,\mathbf X_n]=\boldsymbol\tau_n\) and \[R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)=d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)-(N/n)^2E_{S_m}d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)+(N/n)^2E\{V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\delta_m,\beta)-V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta),\beta)\}.\] This identity remains exact under randomized ties and unequal \(\pi_{iq}\), a case not represented by the ordinary symmetric factorial estimator of Branson, Dasgupta, and Rubin.
body.justification: Exact centering isolates pilot opportunity cost from learned-action regret without symmetry assumptions.
body.gap: Horvitz and Thompson give fixed-design unbiasedness, while Branson, Dasgupta, and Rubin use symmetric factorial rerandomization; neither supplies this pilot-conditional pooled identity under a learned unequal-inclusion law.
body.consumer: It permits unbiased reuse of both waves in sequential factorial cycles whose learned acceptance rule is not label symmetric.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(w_q=2^{1-K_f}c_q\).  First fix a nonempty balanced set \(T\), a legal action \(H\), and a realized potential-outcome table.  The support floor in \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}mixture}\) gives
\[
 p_{T,H}(z)\geq \frac{\eta}{|\Omega_T|},
 \qquad
 \pi_{iq}(T,H)\geq \frac{\eta}{Q}>0.
\]
The second inequality follows because exactly \(|\Omega_T|/Q\) balanced assignments put unit \(i\) at treatment combination \(q\).  Thus every division in the Horvitz--Thompson formula is valid.  By the definition of \(\pi_{iq}(T,H)\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_{p_{T,H}}\!\left[\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(H)\mid \mathbf Y_n,\mathbf X_n\right]
 &=\frac1{|T|}\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
 w_qY_{in}(q)\frac{P_{p_{T,H}}(Z_i=q)}{\pi_{iq}(T,H)}\\
 &=\frac1{|T|}\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}w_qY_{in}(q)
 =\boldsymbol\tau_T.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This calculation uses neither label symmetry nor equality of the first-order inclusion probabilities.

For a fixed split \(S=S_m\), write \(T=S^c\) and
\[
 e_S=\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_S(0)-\boldsymbol\tau_S,
 \qquad
 e_T=\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(\delta_m)-\boldsymbol\tau_T.
\]
The finite-population identity
\[
 \boldsymbol\tau_n=\frac mn\boldsymbol\tau_S+\frac Nn\boldsymbol\tau_T
\]
follows directly by partitioning the unit sum.  Conditional on \(S\), the full potential-outcome table, and the pilot sigma-field \(\mathcal O_m\), the action \(\delta_m\) is fixed and the preceding Horvitz--Thompson calculation gives \(E(e_T\mid S,\mathbf Y_n,\mathbf X_n,\mathcal O_m)=0\).  Since \(e_S\) is measurable with respect to these conditioning variables,
\[
 E(e_S^{\mathsf T}We_T\mid S,\mathbf Y_n,\mathbf X_n,\mathcal O_m)=0.
\]
Consequently, after averaging over the outcome law in \(\mathrm{ass{:}stable\text{-}product\text{-}law}\),
\[
 R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)
 =\left(\frac mn\right)^2E_{S_m}V_{S_m}(0,\beta)
 +\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\delta_m,\beta).
 \tag{1}
\]
The product law is used here only to ensure that, conditional on the split, the unobserved main-wave outcome table has its stated conditional law independently of the pilot outcomes on which \(\delta_m\) depends.  The conditional centering itself was design based and held for every fixed table.

It remains to identify the complete-randomization part of (1).  When \(H=0\), all imbalance scores tie, so the common boundary randomization has \(a_{T,0}(z)=\alpha\) for every \(z\in\Omega_T\).  Hence \(p_{T,0}\) is uniform on \(\Omega_T\) and \(\pi_{iq}(T,0)=1/Q\).  Generate a uniform \(m\)-subset, independently assign its units uniformly over its balanced support, and do the same on its complement.  For any fixed \(z\in\Omega_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}\), the number of compatible pilot subsets is
\[
 \prod_{q\in\mathcal Q}{n/Q\choose m/Q},
\]
which does not depend on \(z\).  Therefore the combined assignment is uniform on \(\Omega_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}\).  Moreover, the two weighted wave estimators combine pointwise to the full-sample Horvitz--Thompson estimator because
\[
 \frac mn\frac1m\sum_{i\in S}\sum_q\frac{w_q\mathbf 1\{Z_i=q\}Y_{in}(q)}{1/Q}
 +\frac Nn\frac1N\sum_{i\in T}\sum_q\frac{w_q\mathbf 1\{Z_i=q\}Y_{in}(q)}{1/Q}
 =\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_q\frac{w_q\mathbf 1\{Z_i=q\}Y_{in}(q)}{1/Q}.
\]
Applying the already proved cross-term cancellation with both actions equal to zero yields
\[
 V_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(0,\beta)
 =\left(\frac mn\right)^2E_{S_m}V_{S_m}(0,\beta)
 +\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E_{S_m}V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(0,\beta).
 \tag{2}
\]
Subtract \(R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)=V_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(G_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta),\beta)\) from (1), substitute (2), and add and subtract \((N/n)^2E V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta),\beta)\).  The definition of \(d_T\) then gives exactly
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)
 &=d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)
 -\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E_{S_m}d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)\\
 &\quad+\left(\frac Nn\right)^2E\!\left[
 V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\delta_m,\beta)
 -V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta),\beta)
 \right].
 \end{aligned}
\]
Randomized boundary ties affect only the numerical values of \(p_{T,H}\) and \(\pi_{iq}\), not any equality above.  Unequal inclusion probabilities are retained in every inverse-probability factor.  An ordinary symmetric estimator replaces those factors by the common value \(Q\), so it does not represent the unequal-inclusion case in general.
